data.title: Bake a high-detail prop onto a game mesh
data.summary: One high-detail panel, a low-detail panel, a non-overlapping UV map and a 1024 px normal target. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Cycles can bake shading information into image textures.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender → Godot or Unity environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: One high-detail panel, a low-detail panel, a non-overlapping UV map and a 1024 px normal target.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent normal bake prop workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: One high-detail panel, a low-detail panel, a non-overlapping UV map and a 1024 px normal target. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Align high and low meshes; set the low mesh's active image target
Bake selected-to-active tangent normals with a cage or bounded extrusion
Load the low mesh and normal texture in the target shader; compare under a moving light

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned bake a high-detail prop onto a game mesh candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: No cage projection leaks across the panel edge
Flat faces remain flat and bevel shading agrees with the high mesh
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A normal map cannot reproduce the source silhouette or physical relief.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.

tips: Use a clearly named non-color normal image and inspect tangent convention.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me bake a high-detail prop onto a game mesh in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: One high-detail panel, a low-detail panel, a non-overlapping UV map and a 1024 px normal target. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: No cage projection leaks across the panel edge; Flat faces remain flat and bevel shading agrees with the high mesh. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
